cands.name: Steve Hurst

money.note: Covers January 2023 on, primary and general. Party-committee lines are often in-kind staff and mail.

cands.bio: Republican member of the Alabama House of Representatives for District 35, serving since 1998. Worked for Georgia Pacific Corporation. Graduated from Talladega High School. Has served as vice chair of the Agriculture and Forestry Committee. Sponsored the state's chemical castration measure for sex offenders, which passed in 2019.
cands.gaps: The pages available did not show Steve Hurst's birthplace, upbringing, or when he came to Alabama; Wikipedia gives only an approximate birth year of 1948. No Ballotpedia Candidate Connection survey, campaign site, interview or questionnaire was available, so no stated positions were found on data centers, homestead taxes, land ownership, growth, immigration, donor money, policing, guns, abortion or school choice. No bill he sponsored or action he took on those topics could be confirmed from the pages read. No documented stances on data centers or development were found. No controversies, foreign ties or endorsements of him were found. Ballotpedia says it found no endorsements for him in 2026. His sponsored-bill list on Ballotpedia did not load in the text available.

cands.bio: Independent candidate for Alabama House District 35 in 2026. Works as a machinist and union member at a local foundry and previously worked at the Anniston Army Depot. He has not held public office.
cands.gaps: We found no record of Cleveland holding any elected office, so there is no legislative record to review. His birthplace is not stated in the pages we read, and his residence history comes only from his campaign site. We found no stated positions from him on data centers, development, homestead taxes, land ownership, immigration or H-1B, policing, guns, abortion, school choice or teacher pay. His campaign site lists these priorities: public rate hearings for Public Service Commission decisions, repealing Alabama's right-to-work amendment, newer school buses with heat and air conditioning, and ending the grocery tax. He did not complete Ballotpedia's candidate survey. We found no documented controversies, foreign ties or endorsements.

local.label: Roots 90: His campaign site says he has lived in the community his entire life and attended school in Munford and Talladega, but it does not state his birthplace.
